scoring_justification: Headline quantities are computed core energies and decomposition confirmation from EAM simulation; full recompute from raw atomic configurations is infeasible in verifier sandbox, so T0 result-level comparison against paper-reported values with tolerance is used.

outputs.description: Core energy of the perfect a[01-1] edge dislocation in NiAl computed within a 9 nm radius. The value will be compared to the paper-reported result within an appropriate tolerance.

Core energy (9 nm radius), separation between a<010> dislocation cores, and boolean confirmation for the decomposed a[01-1] edge configuration. Energy and separation are compared to paper values within tolerances, and the boolean must be true.

output_contract.notes: The agent must obtain the Rao et al. (1991) EAM potential from the public literature (or equivalent published parameters). The workflow is purely computational; no experimental TEM images or weak-beam simulations are required. All necessary elastic constants are stated in the resources.

steps.description: Check perfect core radius=9.0 nm and energy within 10% of paper value 4.2e-9 J/m
Check decomposed core radius=9.0 nm, energy within 10% of 3.6e-9 J/m, separation in [0.1,20] nm, and decomposition_confirmed==true
Check that decomposed core energy is strictly less than perfect core energy

hidden_assets.purpose: Paper-reported core energies: perfect 4.2e-9 J/m, decomposed 3.6e-9 J/m
hidden_assets.source_provenance: From paper text: 'For a radius of 9 nm, the energy of the relaxed, perfect core ... is 4.2×10^-9 J m^-1, while the energy for the decomposed core is 3.6×10^-9 J m^-1.'
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Directly quoted from peer-reviewed published result
